quotes.text: A passkey is a matched pair of keys, and the two of them do very different jobs. One key is private. It lives on your device and it never leaves.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Simple explanation of the key pair behind every passkey.

quotes.text: Phishing works by getting you to hand over a secret, and a passkey leaves you with no secret to hand over.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States in one line why passkeys are phishing resistant.

quotes.text: Microsoft's own guidance points to synced passkeys because they're convenient. They survive a lost device, and they still stop phishing.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation on which passkey type suits most users.

quotes.text: Passkeys don't expire on their own, so there's no built in clock forcing a refresh, and Microsoft recommends keeping an eye on them over time.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical lifecycle advice that is easy to overlook.

quotes.text: The honest summary is this passkeys removed the single biggest way accounts get taken over and they don't fix everything.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Balanced verdict on what passkeys do and do not solve.

takeaways: A passkey is a key pair whose private half never leaves your device, so there is no shared secret that a phishing page could steal.
Synced passkeys suit most users because they survive a lost device, while administrators and privileged accounts should use device-bound passkeys such as security keys or Microsoft Authenticator.
Passkeys are becoming the default sign-in in Microsoft Entra ID, so set up a backup passkey early and plan for limits such as visibility of synced copies.
hook: Passwords and one-time codes can still be phished, and Microsoft is now making passkeys the default sign-in for Microsoft 365. This Simply Explained episode is for everyday users and IT admins who want to understand passkeys and FIDO2 without the jargon. You will learn how passkeys work, which type to choose and what to plan for before rolling them out.
